outputs.L1:
Here are two polished versions of the text depending on your intended context. 

---

### Option 1: Polished Poetic Verse
*This version preserves the original rhyming structure, rhythm, and classical poetic elegance while modernizing spelling, punctuation, and syntax for seamless readability.*

> Time, the sole cause of my unrest,  
> By whom I hoped once to be blessed,  
> How cruel you have turned!  
> You first gave life unto my love,  
> And made it sweet, never to move  
> Or change, though ever burned.  
> 
> Have I neglected you, or left undone  
> One loving rite, that I have won  
> Your rage and bitter change?  
> That now no minute I may see  
> Wherein I might yet happy be,  
> Your favors grown so strange?  
> 
> Blame then yourself, and not my folly;  
> Time grants us time but to be holy—  
> True love such ends approves.  
> Unworthy love seeks selfish ends,  
> But worthy love to worth pretends,  
> Nor other passion proves.  
> 
> Then stay your swiftness, cruel Time,  
> And let me once more blessed climb  
> To joy, that I may praise thee.  
> Let me sweet pleasure fully taste,  
> In faithful love that will not waste,  
> And on Fame’s wings I’ll raise thee.  
> 
> Your dying glory none shall see  
> Until your own final untying,  
> When Time no longer lives.  
> 'Tis gain such precious time to lend,  
> For so your fame shall never end,  
> But joy in what it gives.

---

### Option 2: Elegant Prose Adaptation
*This version translates the poem into sophisticated, professional modern prose while retaining every original nuance, argument, and theme.*

> Time, the sole source of my distress—from whom I once hoped to receive blessing—how cruel you have become. You initially gave life to my devotion, granting a steadfast constancy that remains unyielding even while consumed by longing.
>
> Have I neglected my duties or omitted any sacred rite of love to earn your wrath and bitter shift? Now, not a single minute brings me even the slightest happiness, so completely have your favors been withdrawn.
>
> Blame yourself, therefore, and not my foolishness. Time was granted solely to be held sacred—an ideal that true love cherishes most. Unworthy love pursues self-serving ends, whereas noble love aims only for true merit, harboring no lesser thoughts.
>
> Halt your swift passage, cruel Time, and allow me once more to ascend to a blessed state of joy, so that I may sing your praises. Let me taste sweet delight, rejoicing in a love of unfailing fidelity, and I shall elevate your renown upon the wings of fame.
>
> Your glory shall never fade until the very end of all things, when Time itself ceases to be. It is a rich investment to grant such moments, for through them your legacy will endure forever, celebrating the very joy it bestows.

outputs.L3:
Here is a complete, well-structured expansion of the provided points:

***

At the heart of the speaker’s profound distress lies a bitter betrayal by Time itself. The speaker attributes their current agony to this relentless force, which once acted as a gentle patron to their affection. In the beginning, Time nurtured and fostered a deep, unchanging devotion, allowing their affection to take root and blossom. Now, however, Time has turned inexplicably cruel, withdrawing its favors and leaving the speaker stranded in a landscape of sorrow, mourning the lost grace of happier days.

Faced with this sudden hostility, the speaker passionately defends their own conduct, refusing to accept that their suffering is self-inflicted. They assert their absolute innocence, insisting that they have faithfully performed every duty required by love. Through every trial, their devotion has remained steadfast and pure. Having committed no fault nor yielded to any weakness, the speaker maintains that they have done nothing to deserve the bitter, punishing turn that Time has taken against them.

To emphasize the injustice of their plight, the speaker elevates the nature of their affection, drawing a clear line between their own noble devotion and the superficial impulses of unworthy love. While lesser affections may be driven by selfish desire or fleeting passions, the speaker declares that true love is sacred, selfless, and untainted by base motives. Because their love remains holy and steadfast, it deserves to be cherished and protected by the universe, rather than crushed by temporal decay.

Driven by the sanctity of this bond, the speaker turns directly to their tormentor with a poignant entreaty. They plead with cruel Time to halt its swift, destructive progression and grant a respite from its relentless march. The speaker begs for the restoration of their lost joy, asking Time to create a peaceful space where their faithful love might once again flourish free from the shadow of despair.

In a final, compelling offer of reconciliation, the speaker proposes a grand bargain. If Time will grant them mercy and restore their happiness, the speaker promises to become Time’s ultimate champion. Through the power of their art and devotion, they vow to sing Time’s praises and elevate its fame across the ages. By immortalizing Time’s benevolence in song, the speaker ensures that the glory of Time itself will never fade, turning a plea for personal joy into a monument of eternal praise.
outputs.L4:
To the heart anchored in a deep and faithful affection, there is no tyrant more ruthless than the silent, unceasing march of Time. To watch the precious hours erode the landscape of love—stealing youth, stretching distances, and threatening to wither the vibrant joy shared between two devoted souls—is to endure a profound and agonizing grief. Burdened by this distress, the speaker refuses to sink into quiet despair. Instead, she turns her gaze directly toward her antagonist, stepping into the realm of poetic invocation to confront personified Time face-to-face.

Standing before this ancient, unyielding force, the speaker raises her voice not in futile anger, but in a desperate and eloquent plea. She implores the swift-winged sovereign of seconds to halt his relentless progress, to stay his destructive scythe, and to allow her love a moment of sanctuary from his ravages. Yet, knowing that Time yields to no ordinary tears, she presents a bold and desperate proposition: a solemn bargain. In exchange for the restoration and preservation of her love's stolen joy, she promises to dedicate her art to Time itself. She offers to build him a monument of gilded verse, weaving his name into songs of eternal praise that will echo far beyond the span of mortal lives.

In framing this daring pact, the speaker unveils a profound truth about the nature of genuine affection. Superficial passions may crumble under the slightest weight of years, but a love that is true, noble, and unwavering possesses a transcendent quality that inherently defies temporal decay. While the physical world crumbles around it, the spirit of faithful love remains untouchable by the hourglass. By refusing to let her devotion be consumed by the grave, the speaker demonstrates that true love belongs not to the fleeting realm of flesh and dust, but to the domain of the everlasting.

Ultimately, this proposed covenant establishes a majestic, reciprocal relationship between the mortal artist and the immortal conqueror. Time, though mighty, is blind and indifferent; without the voice of the poet, his vast conquests fade into the dark oblivion of forgotten history. By offering her poetic devotion, the speaker grants Time something he cannot grant himself: immortal glory and honored remembrance in human memory. In return, Time is asked to yield his dominion over her heart, granting the lover the everlasting joy she so fiercely defends. Through the sacred medium of art, the speaker thus transforms a tale of suffering into a monument of triumph, proving that love and poetry together can tame the infinite, securing joy for the heart while granting eternal life to Time itself.
outputs.L5:
**Time** is perhaps the most mysterious currency we possess. We cannot save it in a bank, nor can we buy more of it when our balance runs low. It flows endlessly forward, completely indifferent to our plans, desires, or regrets.

It is remarkable **how** our perception of these passing seconds changes depending on where we stand in life. When we are young, a single summer feels endless, stretching out like a vast horizon of possibility. Yet, as the years accumulate, whole seasons seem to blur together in the blink of an eye. We often wonder **how** a single hour can move so agonizingly slowly during moments of waiting, yet sprint past us when we are surrounded by laughter and love.

It is in these quiet reflections **that** we discover the true value of our existence. We come to realize **that** yesterday is merely a memory, and tomorrow is nothing more than an unwritten promise. The fundamental truth remains **that** the only moment we ever truly inhabit is right now.

Ultimately, we cannot control the relentless ticking of the clock, but we can control **how** we choose to live within its rhythm. When we finally accept **that** **time** is both finite and fleeting, every shared story, quiet breath, and humble morning light becomes an extraordinary gift.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a Renaissance-style love poem addressing personified Time in Early Modern English spelling, complaining about how Time has turned against the speaker's love.
counterfactuals.output:
O cruell Tyme, that once didst smyle so faire,
Vpon the blooming morning of my loue,
Why dost thou now bring cloudes of darke despaire,
And turne thy swift-wing'd houres against my Doue?

Thy envious Sithe doth hunt her rosie Cheeke,
To steale the orient Luster from her Eye,
And make that Hart, which late was soft and meeke,
As colde as Marble 'neath a wintry Skie.

Thou wert the Poost of all our sweete Delight,
When first we swore our Vowes in Louers' Shade;
Now like a Theefe thou robb'st me in the Night,
Vnmaking all the Ioyes that thou hast made.

Yet rage thy fill, false Tyme, with all thy Might:
Thou canst not quench our Loue's eternall Light.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a poem in 17th century spelling about cruell time ruining a lover's happiness.
counterfactuals.output:
O cruell Tyme! why hast thou stolne away
The golden Promise of our sweetest Day?
When in the Bower of my True-Loues imbrace,
I read all Heauen in her Angell face.

Then did the Rose vpon her Cheeke abide,
And Ioy sate smiling at my Faire-One's side;
No anxious Thought did marre our chaste Delight,
Nor darke Suspition of approaching Night.

But thou, relentlesse Tyrant, keene and cold,
Hast turn'd our shining Youth to Ashes old!
Thy greedy Sythe hath mow'd our Blisse away,
And wrapt our Sunshine in a sad Decay.

Her vermeil Lips, where Kisses wont to dwell,
Are toucht by Thee with Age his dolesome Spell;
The christall Luster of her Eye is fled,
And all the Garland of our Hope is dead.

Thou swift-foot Theefe, that stealest in the Darke,
To quench of Cupid's Fire the smallest Sparke!
Thou hast undone the Knot that Loue had ty'd,
And left a Wretch where stood a happy Bride.

Now nought remaines but Sorrow and Despaire,
To testifie how Blest two Lovers were;
Ah, cruell Tyme! that brought so sweet a Grace,
Onely to spill it in so short a Space.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

Theme: The speaker begs Time to halt its swiftness, reflecting on true love versus unworthy love, and promises to immortalize Time's fame if granted joy.
counterfactuals.output:
O Tyrant Time, staye thy swift-wingèd flight,
And turne to Shade this burning Beame of light;
Why dost thou haste, when joy is scarsely knowne,
And reape the Seed before the Flowre bee blowne?
I begge thee, pause, and let thy Scythe lye still,
Nor serve so cruell and so swift a Will.

Thou fly’st too fast when Sweetnesse doth appeare,
Yet creep’st like Ice through every dismall Yeare.
O checke thy Course, and graunt my panting Brest
A quiet Hour to taste of Love’s blest Rest;
For False Love fades like Shadowes on the Greene,
Where fleeting Fancies only once have beene.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an Elizabethan verse lament where a heart-broken lover addresses Time, asking why their faithful devotion has been met with bitter change, and offering eternal praise if Time stays its swift pace.
counterfactuals.output:
O churlish Time, that swift in flight dost glide,
Why hast thou struck my true and faithful heart?
Upon Love’s altar did my faith abide,
Yet thou hast slain my joy with bitter dart.
Why should devotion yield a crop of grief,
And constant truth find no sweet balm’s relief?

No fleeting fancy did my soul beguile,
Nor base desire that perishes in night;
Yet thou hast stolen my fair lady’s smile,
And turned my golden noon to sudden blight.
Was all my truth but fuel for thy decay,
To melt like frost before a cruel day?

O stay thy chariot! Hold thy glass of sand!
Suffer thy hungry sickle now to rest!
Reach forth no more thy cold, unsparing hand
To freeze the gentle spring within her breast.
Turn back the shadow on the sunlit dial,
And grant my weeping love a gracious while.

If thou wilt stay thy sharp and rusting blade,
And mend the bond that thou hast torn apart,
A monument of verse shall thee be made,
To praise thy mercy to the human heart.
No tyrant shall men call thee with their tongue,
But gentle Time, forever blessed and young.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem to Time in the voice of a Jacobean poet with original spellings intact.
counterfactuals.output:
**To the All-Devouring Tyrant, Time**

O cruell Tyrant of the fleeting Yeere,
That steal’st vpon our Ioyes with wingèd Feete,
Thou mak’st the fairest Beautie disappeare,
And sour’st the Nectar that was once so sweete.

Thy Glasse of Sand doth trickle without Stay,
Thy crooked Sithe mowes downe the blushing Rose;
The proudest Monarch must thy Will obey,
And yeeld his Crowne when-as thy Shadow growes.

Yet though thy Teeth deuoure this mortall Clay,
And turne our glorious Trophies into Dust,
Thou canst not snatch my true-Love’s Heart away,
Nor rust the Faith wherein the Righteous trust.

Then haste thee, Time, and runne thy greedy Race,
Spend all thy Sand, and let thy Chariot flye;
For when I meete my Maker face to face,
Thou shalt be Dead, and I no more shall dye.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
